name: つじ田 神田御茶ノ水店
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町1-4 和田ビル 1F
cuisine: The original つじ田 — the shop that opened here in 2005 and made 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 a Tokyo genre. Sixteen counter seats, thick noodles into a heavy pork-and-dried-fish dip, finished at the table with sudachi and coarse black pepper; ¥1,000–¥1,999, no reservations, served until it runs out.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 1-chōme — 27 m from Ogawamachi station (Toei Shinjuku line): out of exit A7 and 40 m to the left. The same exits serve Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line) and Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), and JR Ochanomizu is a short walk north.

gf_detail: Ruled out by the operator's own allergen statement, not just by inference. つじ田's parent オイシーズ株式会社 (Oishes) publishes a group allergy page saying 「当店の厨房設備及び商品の製造上、アレルギー食材を完全に除くことができません」, that every dish is cooked with the same utensils so ingredients not belonging to a dish can transfer, and that 「麺、スープ等の製造工場では、小麦、卵、乳成分を原材料とする商品の製造を行ってます」 — the noodle and soup plant itself handles wheat, egg and dairy. It adds that the company may decline to serve customers who react to trace amounts. On top of that the product is wheat tsukemen noodles in a wheat-shōyu-based dip. There is no gluten-free item.

roles: 創業者・店主 (founder; the brand is operated by オイシーズ株式会社 / Oishes Inc.)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Ogawamachi, Chiyoda-ku — this shop is the brand's birthplace
chef_bio.background: つじ田 opened at Kanda-Ochanomizu in 2005 and is the shop the company itself credits with leading Tokyo's tsukemen culture: 「味から絆へ、2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」. From this 16-seat counter the brand grew into a nationwide group — Kōjimachi, Shinbashi, Iidabashi, Nihonbashi-Yaesu, Shibuya Fukuras, Suidōbashi, Ningyōchō, Ōtemachi One, Kachidoki, Tōyōchō, Ikebukuro, Osaka Higobashi and Expocity, and Fukuoka airport — plus two spin-off lines, つじ田 味噌の章 (a miso-ramen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2009, three Tokyo shops) and 成都正宗担々麺 (a tantanmen specialist opened in Ogawamachi in 2016). The stated house principle is that the recipe is never finished: 「濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺のパイオニアであるつじ田のこだわりは、常においしさを求めて進化を続けること」. The Kanda-Ochanomizu shop stays deliberately plain — counter only, cash with no electronic money, no reservations, unpredictable closing days, and it stops when the soup goes.
chef_bio.philosophy: 常においしさを求めて進化を続けること — keep evolving in pursuit of flavour; 「こだわりがあるからこそ、はじめてお客様に愛される」.
chef_bio.specialty: 濃厚豚骨魚介つけ麺 — the thick pork-and-fish tsukemen the brand pioneered, eaten with sudachi and coarse black pepper.

anecdotes.text: The company dates the whole tsukemen brand to this address: 「2005年神田御茶ノ水でオープンして以来、味へ圧倒的なこだわりで東京のつけ麺文化を牽引」.
Tabelog's directions are unusually precise about how close it is — out of Ogawamachi exit A7, turn left, 40 m; the station is 27 m away.

cultural_comfort.note: Twenty-seven metres from Ogawamachi station, so it is essentially impossible to miss: exit A7, turn left. Ordering is counter service on effectively one dish, so no Japanese is needed; the table ritual — squeeze the sudachi, grind the pepper — is worth copying from the person next to you. If you are avoiding egg or dairy rather than wheat, the operator's allergy page at oishes.com/allergy is genuinely usable.

name: つけ麺 素家
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-24 大栄堂第２ビル 1F
cuisine: A ten-seat one-man tsukemen counter serving a deliberately retro 豚骨魚介 dip — thick straight Taisei-Shokuhin noodles, chāshū, menma, naruto and negi all sunk in the bowl — with the house trick being a 自家製りんご甘酢, a sweet apple vinegar you pour over the noodles before dipping. つけ麺 ¥1,100, らーめん ¥1,050, 油そば ¥1,050; 200 g regular and 300 g large cost the same.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 3-chōme — 313 m from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line); about 4 minutes from the shared B5 exit that also serves Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku line) and Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line). Look for the building with the acoustic-guitar shop en.guitar lit up behind its second-floor window; the shop is the ground floor, in the former premises of 一挙一会.
gf_detail: No. The shop sells three dishes and all three are wheat noodles — the tsukemen and abura-soba use 200–300 g of thick straight noodles made by 大成食品, and the dip is described by reviewers as a 豚骨魚介醤油 tare, i.e. wheat soy sauce. There is no allergen information, no gluten-free claim, one boiler and one person working the whole counter, so there is no separable line even in principle.
vegan_detail: No. The dip is a pork-bone-and-dried-fish broth and every bowl comes with chāshū, menma and naruto (fish cake) already in it; the side menu is a chāshū rice bowl. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 店主 (owner-chef, works the shop single-handed)
chef_bio.origin: Trained at 麺彩房 — the Nakano ramen house whose 豚骨魚介 style he still cooks
chef_bio.background: 素家 is fifteen years old and on its third address. It opened in Asakusabashi on 1 December 2010 under an owner who came out of 麺彩房, moved to Iidabashi on 26 March 2019, and moved again to Kanda-Ogawamachi on 17 October 2025, taking over the ground-floor unit that used to be 一挙一会. The current shop is an irregular U-shaped counter of ten seats (3-1-3-3) wrapped around the kitchen, worked by the owner alone — reviewers single out how quietly courteous the service is for a one-man ramen counter. The bowl is unfashionably old-school: a thick, glossy pork-and-fish shōyu dip that a veteran reviewer recognised immediately as 麺彩房's, with the noodles supplied, as at 麺彩房, by 大成食品. The one flourish is on the table — alongside the fish powder, vinegar and S&B ichimi sits a house-made apple sweet-vinegar that the shop tells you to pour straight onto the noodles; it reads as apple juice with a faint tartness rather than as vinegar. Soup-thinning dashi is left on the table in a pot. Tabelog rates it 3.37 and the shop posts on X as @soyatsuke; there is no telephone number on file.
chef_bio.specialty: つけ麺 ¥1,100 — 200 g regular or 300 g large at the same price — eaten first plain, then with the 自家製りんご甘酢, then finished with the table-side soup-splitting dashi.

anecdotes.text: A long-running Tokyo ramen blogger arrived ten minutes before the evening opening on 20 October 2025, three days after the shop moved in, and was first in a queue of three. His verdict on the dip: 「まんまは『麺彩房』譲りの味わい。ノス感あるレトロな豚魚つけ麺ですが、大変丁寧にしっかりと作り込まれていてとっても美味しい」.
The house serving suggestion is unusual enough that reviewers make a point of it — pour the 自家製りんご甘酢 directly over the noodles before dipping: 「りんご甘酢は全然酸っぱくなくて、りんご果汁にほのかな酸味的な、糖度多めの甘酸っぱい味わい」.

name: お茶の水、大勝軒
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-1-5 須田ビル 1F
cuisine: A direct 暖簾分け of the vanished 東池袋大勝軒, run by a disciple who was told by Yamagishi himself never to change the taste — so the 特製もりそば here is the original tsukemen: hand-cut, chewy noodles chilled then dipped back in hot water, into a collagen-heavy sweet-sour-shōyu dip. It also serves a 1954 Shōwa-era curry that won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix, and from the afternoon a 復刻版 menu of dishes sealed away when the old shop closed. ¥1,000–¥1,999.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 3-chōme — 5 minutes from Jimbōchō (Toei Mita, Toei Shinjuku, Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines, 363 m), 5 minutes from Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku) and Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 6 minutes from JR Ochanomizu.
hours_raw: 11:00～21:00 ＜17時より復刻版（Classic）メニューもご提供します＞　定休日：月曜日（月曜日が祝日の場合は火曜日）、年始・お盆　※まれに貸切宴会のときがありますのでご注意下さい（SNSでお知らせあり）
gf_detail: No, on several counts at once. The noodles are wheat; the shop's own description of the 特製もりそば calls the dip a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour edge, i.e. wheat soy sauce; the 復刻版カレー中華 is finished with 醤油だれ and 水溶き片栗粉 over the curry roux; and the celebrated curry is explicitly thickened 「小麦粉とスパイスで仕上げた」 — wheat flour in the roux itself. The gyōza wrappers are made in-house from wheat flour and the shop also serves wontons and shūmai. No allergen statement and no gluten-free item exists.
vegan_detail: No. The stock is the 丸長 lineage 中華そば broth — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi layered over it, which is the shop's whole historical claim — so even the vegetable-forward 復刻版タンメン is built on animal and fish stock and stir-fried with pork. The house まかない飯 is chāshū fried with raw egg. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 山岸一雄の弟子 (disciple of Kazuo Yamagishi, granted 暖簾分け)
chef_bio.origin: Minami-Ōtsuka, Toshima-ku — he grew up a short walk from the old Higashi-Ikebukuro Taishōken
chef_bio.background: The Taishōken line runs 丸長 (Ogikubo, 1948, founded by the Shinshū soba craftsman 青木勝治, who first put niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi into a Chinese-style broth) → 栄楽 → 中野大勝軒 (1951, named for the wish 「大きく軒並みに勝る」) → 東池袋大勝軒 (1961), where 山岸一雄 turned the staff-meal つけそば into the 特製もりそば of 1955 and, in doing so, invented tsukemen as a commercial dish. Over about twenty years Yamagishi granted around a hundred 暖簾分け, and their own disciples take the family past two hundred shops; the Higashi-Ikebukuro original closed in March 2007 to redevelopment and Yamagishi's failing health. 田内川真介 grew up in Minami-Ōtsuka and had been eating there since boyhood, treated by Yamagishi 「実の子供のように」; in 1995, aged eighteen and in his first year of university, he became the old shop's first-ever part-timer. He took a salaried job after graduating, quit it because he wanted to preserve Yamagishi's taste, and went back to be taken on as a formal apprentice. He was granted 暖簾分け after about eighteen months but kept training while he looked for premises, and opened お茶の水、大勝軒 in September 2006 with Yamagishi supervising the reconstruction of the old Higashi-Ikebukuro flavour. Yamagishi's parting words before opening — 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ。」 — are the shop's governing instruction, and it has since become one of the family's designated keepers of the 復刻版 (Classic) menu, reviving dishes the old shop had sealed away, reproduced to the original recipes under Yamagishi's own supervision. Its Shōwa-era curry, created by Yamagishi in 1954 at Nakano out of his memory of navy curry, took 準グランプリ at the 2016 神田カレーグランプリ and the outright グランプリ in 2017, with a further 準グランプリ and the Meister Prize in 2019 for a dry keema. The shop now anchors a small group including 大勝軒next and 山ノ内大勝軒 in Yamagishi's birthplace under Shiga Kōgen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ」 — Yamagishi's instruction not to change the taste. The shop treats that as covering not only Yamagishi's own cooking but the 栄楽 and 中野大勝軒 traditions behind it.
chef_bio.specialty: 特製もりそば — the original tsukemen, hand-cut chewy noodles chilled and then passed back through hot water so the dip stays hot; 復刻版タンメン, 復刻版カレー中華 (Yamagishi's own invention at twenty, from his father's navy curry), 復刻版ワンタン/ワンタンメン/シュウマイ and the all-day 餃子; the Kanda Curry Grand Prix-winning curry; and the まかない飯, block-cut chāshū fried with egg and spring onion.

anecdotes.text: Tsukemen exists because a customer looked over the counter. Yamagishi was eating the staff-meal つけそば out of sight in the kitchen when a regular said 「うまそうじゃないの。おれたちにも食わせてよ」; he tried it on a few people, the reaction was good, and it went on the menu in 1955 as 特製もりそば.
The dish began as thrift, not invention: in the post-war food shortage wheat flour was too precious to throw away, so 青木勝治 devised a way to eat the noodles left in the zaru 「ざるそば気分で」.
Tauchigawa was the old Higashi-Ikebukuro shop's first part-time employee, hired in 1995 at eighteen; he later quit a company job to come back as an apprentice.

The curry is older than the tsukemen — Yamagishi built it in 1954 as manager of Nakano Taishōken from his memory of the navy curry his father brought home, and it won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix outright in 2017.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One kitchen turning out wheat noodles, hand-made wheat gyōza and wontons, shūmai and a flour-thickened curry roux. No allergen information is published and no wheat-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop describes the 特製もりそば dip as a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour note — ordinary wheat soy sauce, with no tamari mentioned.
The 復刻版カレー中華 is finished by combining 醤油だれ, potato-starch slurry and spring onion in the soup before the curry roux goes on top.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house broth is the 丸長 lineage stock — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi — so fish is in the base of everything, including the vegetable-heavy 復刻版タンメン, which is also stir-fried with pork.
The 大勝軒 curry is made by frying pork, onion, carrot and potato in lard and simmering them in the ramen stock.

cultural_comfort.level: Welcoming and self-service — one of the easier famous shops
cultural_comfort.note: This is a ticket-machine shop with an unusual routine: buy the ticket, hand it to the kitchen, take back the stub, and collect your bowl yourself when your number is called. Water, garlic, the soup-splitting dashi and clearing your dishes are also self-service; pepper and a cloth are on each table. Unusually for a ramen counter it has 26 seats including proper tables, takes reservations, welcomes children, and accepts transport IC cards, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay, PayPay and Merpay at a terminal under the ticket machine — but no credit cards. Closed Mondays (Tuesday instead when Monday is a public holiday) and over New Year and Obon, and it very occasionally shuts for a private party, announced on its Instagram. Note the timing on the 復刻版 Classic dishes: the shop's front page says they start at 17:00 while the menu page says 15:00, so if you are coming specifically for the tanmen or the curry-chūka, aim for the evening. No English menu, but the ticket machine and the one-dish nature of もりそば make it manageable.

name: 江戸富士
address_ja: 東京都文京区湯島2-7-7 光ビル 1F

In the evening it works as a sushi counter, where reviewers' bills reach ¥10,000–¥14,999.
neighborhood: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku, near the Japan Football Museum — 485 m and about 7 minutes from JR Ochanomizu (Chūō-Sōbu line), 6 minutes from Ochanomizu on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line, 8 minutes from Suehirochō (Tokyo Metro Ginza line) and about 10 minutes from Yushima (Chiyoda line).
hours_raw: 月・火・水・木・金 11:30 - 14:00／土 12:00 - 14:00／日 定休日　■ ネタが無くなり次第終了　※臨時休業が多いので、電話にて営業確認することが必須
gf_detail: Nothing published either way, and this needs care rather than optimism. The core of the lunch is raw fish and rice, which is not itself a gluten problem, but sushi rice is seasoned with vinegar that is often blended with other seasonings, the soy sauce on the counter will be ordinary wheat shōyu unless the shop says otherwise, and the miso soup at ¥350 is very likely a wheat-containing awase or mugi miso — 麦味噌 is barley. Imitation-crab, tamagoyaki and any simmered anago glaze on a sushi counter all carry wheat as standard. There is no allergen information and no gluten-free claim, and the shop has no website on which to check. It is the kind of place where a chef at the counter could plate sashimi and rice without sauce if asked, so 'ask' rather than 'no' — but ask in Japanese, and ask about the shōyu specifically.
vegan_detail: A sushi and kaisendon house whose entire lunch service is one raw-fish bowl and whose Tabelog profile says 魚料理にこだわる. No vegetable-only or plant-based option is listed anywhere, and any dashi will be katsuo.

roles: 大将・店主 (owner-chef; builds the lunch bowls single-handed)
chef_bio.origin: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku — a ground-floor unit in a residential block behind the Japan Football Museum
chef_bio.background: 江戸富士 is an eleven-seat shop — a seven-seat counter and two tables of four — that behaves like two businesses. Lunch, Monday to Saturday, is a single item: the 江戸富士バラ海鮮丼, thick, generous cuts of sashimi over rice, about ¥2,100, with miso soup at ¥350. It is popular enough that a visitor arriving thirty minutes before opening in December 2023 found roughly fifteen people already waiting — in a queue hidden down the alley to the left of the shop rather than in front of it — and was not seated until about 11:50. The owner makes the bowls alone and the service stops when the fish is gone. In the evening the same room is a sushi-ya with sake the shop takes seriously, reservations accepted, private hire for up to twenty, and a spend that reviewers put at ¥10,000–¥14,999. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB) are taken at dinner only — lunch is cash. Tabelog rates it 3.54 and warns in its own notes that unscheduled closures are frequent enough that phoning ahead on 03-3811-0111 is essential.
chef_bio.specialty: 江戸富士バラ海鮮丼 (about ¥2,100) — the thick-cut sashimi bowl that the lunch queue forms for; add the ¥350 miso soup.

anecdotes.text: The queue is not where you expect it. A December 2023 visitor arrived half an hour early, saw nobody in front of the shop and thought she was first — the fifteen people ahead of her were lined up out of sight in the alley to the left.
Same visit: the room held a broad mix of ages and included Korean tourists, and although the menu is Japanese only, the staff worked through it with gestures rather than turning anyone away.

positives.text: Staff have been observed working patiently through the Japanese-only menu with foreign visitors by gesture rather than turning them away, which is a good sign for making a dietary request understood in person.

cultural_comfort.level: Friendly, but you have to work for the seat
cultural_comfort.note: Phone first — Tabelog's own notes say unscheduled closures are frequent and that confirming by telephone (03-3811-0111) is essential, and there is no website or social account to check instead. For lunch arrive well before 11:30 and look for the queue in the alley to the LEFT of the shop, not in front of it; the fish runs out and the shop closes at 14:00 regardless. Lunch is cash only — the cards (VISA, Master, JCB) are dinner-only — and there is no English menu, only a handwritten Japanese one by the entrance, though staff have a good record of getting through it with gestures. It is a 7-minute walk from JR Ochanomizu through a residential stretch of Yushima near the Japan Football Museum, so allow more time than the distance suggests. Dinner is a different and much more expensive proposition: book, and expect ¥10,000 and up.

name: 誠鮨
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田駿河台4-3 新お茶の水ビル B1F
cuisine: An Edomae sushi counter that has been in the basement of the Shin-Ochanomizu Building since 1981, doing the slow work — simmering, curing, marinating — rather than just slicing. Lunch is a limited-run 特選ちらし at ¥1,300; nigiri sets run ¥3,500 (上) and ¥4,500 (特上) with a soup, おまかせ nigiri ¥6,000, and the 誠 course from ¥12,000 including a drink.
neighborhood: Kanda-Surugadai 4-chōme — one minute from JR Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit (Chūō-Sōbu line) and one minute from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), which is exactly where the light record placed it; 6 minutes from Ochanomizu on the Marunouchi line. The shop is in the basement of the Shin-Ochanomizu Building, 114 m from the station.
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim, no allergen information, and two specific things on this counter make wheat likelier than a diner might assume. First, the shop is proud of exactly the preparations that carry it: it describes doing 「煮る」「締める」「漬け込む」 Edomae work on the fish, and it singles out its かんぴょう — simmered gourd, cooked in soy sauce and mirin — as a house specialty alongside the ガリ. Second, its shari is 「数種類のお酢をオリジナルの配合でブレンド」, a proprietary blend of several vinegars, which is precisely the kind of detail that cannot be assumed wheat-free without asking, since grain vinegars in Japan may be wheat-derived. Nikiri brushed onto nigiri is wheat shōyu unless stated otherwise. Against that, this is a counter with a chef in front of you and a menu that says outright 「ご予算に応じて調理致します」 — they will build to request — so a wheat-avoiding diner has somewhere to start. Ask about the shari blend and the nikiri specifically, and expect the kanpyō and any simmered anago to be off the table.
vegan_detail: An Edomae sushi-ya whose entire identity is fish. Tabelog records 魚料理にこだわる; the course structure runs 先付け・刺身・焼物・煮物・寿司・お椀・デザート and the お椀 will be a katsuo or kombu-and-katsuo dashi. There is no vegetable course and no plant-based option advertised.

roles: 大将・店主 (owner-chef; not named on the shop's site)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Surugadai, Chiyoda-ku — the shop has never moved from the Shin-Ochanomizu Building basement
chef_bio.background: 誠鮨 opened in 1981 (昭和56年) in the basement of the 新お茶の水ビル and has traded there ever since, describing itself as 「地元に愛されて」 — a neighbourhood shop for the offices and hospitals of Surugadai rather than a destination. Its stated principle is a pun on its own name: 「誠実であること」を大切に, keeping faith, applied to the sushi, the room and the service. The kitchen leans on the unglamorous half of Edomae technique — the fish is simmered, cured or marinated over time rather than simply cut, and the shop makes a point that its ガリ and かんぴょう are made in-house with as much care as the fish. The rice is its other claim: a proprietary blend of several vinegars, aimed at a soft mouthfeel that lifts the seafood, and the shari is re-cut twice a day so it is served at the right temperature. The room is dressed seasonally, with craft pieces changed for occasions like Momo-no-sekku and Tango-no-sekku. It seats 24 — a ten-seat counter plus tables — takes reservations, accepts all the major cards, and can be hired for parties of up to fifty. The menu is printed in Japanese and English. Tabelog rates it 3.34, with a dinner spend of ¥10,000–¥14,999 against a ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「誠実であること」 — to be sincere; the shop takes its name as its instruction.
chef_bio.specialty: The lunch-only 特選ちらし at ¥1,300, made in limited numbers and changed with the season; おまかせ寿司 at ¥6,000; the 誠 course from ¥12,000. In-house ガリ and かんぴょう are named by the shop as points of pride.

anecdotes.text: The shop cuts its sushi rice twice a day rather than once, purely so that it reaches the customer at the right temperature.
It sells the side dishes as hard as the fish: 「鮨屋の華である、鮮度のよい厳選した鮨ネタはもちろん自慢ですが、ガリやかんぴょうなど、手間を惜しまず拵えた副菜も当店の自慢です」.

The shari is a proprietary blend of several vinegars — 「数種類のお酢をオリジナルの配合でブレンド」 — whose composition is not published, so it cannot be assumed free of grain-derived vinegar.

vegan_cross_contact.text: An Edomae sushi counter; Tabelog records 魚料理にこだわる and the course runs through sashimi, grilled, simmered, sushi and a soup course. No plant-based option exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop states on its menu page that it will cook to the customer's budget and requirements — 「その他、ご予算に応じて調理致します」 / 'We can arrange the menu on your budget' — which is an opening for a dietary request made at reservation, though nothing about allergies is promised.

positives.text: The menu is published in Japanese and English, so a non-Japanese-speaking diner can at least read what is being offered before asking about it.

cultural_comfort.note: One minute from Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit and one from Shin-Ochanomizu, but it is in a basement — go down into the Shin-Ochanomizu Building rather than looking for a street frontage. The menu is bilingual Japanese/English with prices tax-included, which removes most of the anxiety of a sushi counter; there are tables as well as the ten-seat counter, children are welcomed at every age, and all the major cards are accepted. Lunch is the low-risk way in: the ¥1,300 特選ちらし is made in limited numbers, so go early in the 11:30–14:00 window. Closed Sundays and public holidays. Reservations on 03-3295-8537; the shop says it will build a menu to your budget, which is also the right moment to raise a dietary restriction. It has been here since 1981 and reads as a local office-district shop, not a tourist one.

name: 粋庵
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田淡路町2-105 ワテラスアネックス 0102
cuisine: A wa-modern Japanese restaurant on the Waterras Annex ground floor, opened April 2025: hon-maguro handled by a specialist, Ōmi beef bought from a dedicated supplier, and seasonal tempura, in courses at ¥8,000–¥9,999 for dinner against a ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch, with a serious sake, shōchū and wine list. Twenty-eight seats, private rooms for two to six, and a ¥500 cover.
neighborhood: Kanda-Awajichō 2-chōme, in the Waterras Annex — 3 minutes from JR Ochanomizu (Chūō-Sōbu line), 3 minutes and 240 m from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), 3 minutes from Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line).
gf_detail: Nothing is published about allergens, and the shop's three headline items include one that is flatly out: the 天ぷら it advertises is wheat batter, fried in oil shared with everything else fried that service. The 本マグロ and 近江牛 sides of the menu are more negotiable in principle — but a wa-modern kaiseki kitchen seasons almost everything with wheat shōyu and mirin, and no gluten-free tamari is named. What this restaurant does have that most of the shard does not is the machinery for a conversation: it takes reservations, has private rooms, publishes an English menu, and is a 2025-opened room used for 接待 where dietary requests at booking are routine. Ask when you reserve, name the tempura and the soy sauce explicitly, and treat 'ask' as genuinely open here rather than as a polite no.
vegan_detail: Not advertised, but not obviously impossible. Tabelog records the kitchen as 野菜料理にこだわる as well as 魚料理にこだわる, and the format is a course built around seasonal ingredients, which is the format most able to substitute — but the named draws are tuna and Ōmi beef, and the dashi under a Japanese course is katsuo unless the kitchen is told otherwise. There is no published vegan course and no HappyCow-style listing. A vegan meal here would have to be arranged in advance, in Japanese or through the English menu contact, and confirmed as free of dashi and egg.

roles: 料理長 (head chef; not named on the restaurant's site)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Awajichō, Chiyoda-ku — the Waterras Annex, the retail podium of the Waterras redevelopment beside Ochanomizu
chef_bio.background: 粋庵 opened on 8 April 2025 on the ground floor of the Waterras Annex, the low-rise retail building of the Waterras complex between Ochanomizu and Awajichō. It presents itself as a 和モダン Japanese restaurant built for entertaining — 「接待やデートで使いたい和モダンな和食料理店」 — with three things at the centre of the menu: carefully selected hon-maguro, which the shop says is handled 「職人技でその魅力を最大限に引き出し」; Ōmi beef sourced from a dedicated specialist supplier; and tempura made from whatever is in season. Around that sits a drinks list the restaurant treats as equal billing, with sake, shōchū and wine all flagged by Tabelog as 「こだわる」. The room seats 28 across an eight-seat counter and twenty at tables, with private rooms for two, four and six, and can be taken over for parties up to fifty; there is a projector, power at the seats and free wi-fi, it is wheelchair-accessible, and there is an English menu and a children's menu. Payment is unusually open for a Japanese restaurant of this level — every major card including UnionPay, all the common electronic money, and PayPay, d払い, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay and Merpay — with a ¥500 charge per person and no service charge. Tabelog rates it 3.31, which mostly reflects how new it is.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「心ほどける、粋な味わいとともに」 — the shop's own line: carefully made Japanese food and warm hospitality in a calm room.
chef_bio.specialty: 本マグロ, 近江牛 and seasonal 天ぷら — the three items the restaurant names for itself — served in courses, with a sake and wine list treated as part of the offer.

anecdotes.text: The restaurant describes its own audience plainly: 「接待やデートで使いたい和モダンな和食料理店。厳選した本マグロ、近江牛、四季折々の食材を使った天ぷらを味わえる贅沢なコースが魅力です。」

It is unusually well equipped for a Japanese restaurant — projector, power sockets at the seats, free wi-fi, wheelchair access, an English menu and a children's menu — which is what a Waterras ground-floor unit built for corporate entertaining looks like.

cultural_comfort.level: Among the easiest fine-ish Japanese rooms in the area
cultural_comfort.note: Ground floor of the Waterras Annex, three minutes from Ochanomizu, Shin-Ochanomizu and Awajichō alike — the light record's 「新御茶ノ水駅 (ワテラス)」 is exactly right. There is an English menu, free wi-fi, power at the seats, step-free access and a children's menu, and it takes almost every form of payment including UnionPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay, which makes it unusually low-friction for a visitor. Book: it has 28 seats and private rooms for two to six, and it is a room used for business entertaining, so walk-ins at dinner are a gamble. There is a ¥500 cover per person and no service charge. Closed Sundays and public holidays; Saturday runs a longer lunch (to 15:00) and an earlier dinner (16:00–21:00). Because it opened in April 2025 there is very little independent review coverage yet — the picture here comes from the restaurant's own copy and its Tabelog profile, so treat the food description as the house's claim rather than as a verdict.

name: 日乃屋 本店
address_ja: 〒113-0034 東京都文京区湯島2-2-1 東邦深澤ビル 1F
cuisine: The Yushima original of 日乃屋カレー, the chain that grew from this 19-seat room to about a hundred shops and on to California and Taiwan. The house roux is sold on a single line — 「始まり甘く、後より辛い、余韻残りしカレールウ」, sweet at the first mouthful, hot afterwards, and lingering — and the honten also keeps the chūka-soba and tsukemen the chain shops dropped. Sub-¥1,000.
neighborhood: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku — 405 m and about 6 minutes from JR Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit: north past the Yushima Seidō crossing, over the Shimizuzaka-shita junction and left. About 10 minutes west along Kuramaebashi-dōri from Suehirochō (Tokyo Metro Ginza line).
gf_detail: No, and this one is not close. The company's whole proposition is 「日本のカレー、昔からある皆が食べ慣れた、あの懐かしくも深みのあるカレー」 — Japanese-style curry, which is by definition a roux thickened with wheat flour, and the shop describes the roux as made by its own in-house method with no substitution claimed. The honten additionally boils wheat chūka-soba and tsukemen noodles in the same small kitchen (Tabelog files it as カレー、ラーメン、つけ麺), and the signature item is a breadcrumbed katsu — the 名物カツカレー, now also sold as a 三元豚・プレミアムカツカレー. No allergen information is published on hinoya.jp and no gluten-free item exists at any branch.
vegan_detail: Correcting the light record, which carried vegan_status 'options': nothing supports that. The company describes buying meat from the west of Japan, branded eggs, and vegetables chosen nationally, and the standard bowls are katsu, pork and beef; the honten also runs a chūka-soba stock. A newer 印度式カレー roux is advertised as 「スパイスとベジタブルが効きまくり」, but that is a description of flavour, not a vegan claim, and the site says explicitly that whether a branch carries it varies. No vegan or vegetarian item is listed anywhere on the official site, and Japanese curry roux routinely contains animal extract and honey.

roles: 代表者 (representative director, 有限会社ノアランド / Noahland Ltd.)
chef_bio.origin: Yushima 2-chōme, Bunkyō-ku — the company's registered head office is this building, 東京都文京区湯島2-2-1 東邦深澤ビル1階
chef_bio.background: 有限会社ノアランド was founded in August 2004 and the Yushima honten is both the first 日乃屋カレー and, to this day, the company's registered address — the head office is the shop. The house line, printed at the top of the company's own page, is 「始まり甘く、後より辛い、余韻残りしカレールウ」: sweet at the start, hot afterwards, with an aftertaste that stays. The company is explicit that it is not chasing modern curry styles — 「昨今ありとあらゆるスタイルのカレーが世に出回っていますが、日乃屋は一貫して日本のカレー、昔からある皆が食べ慣れた、あの懐かしくも深みのあるカレーを日々追求しております」 — and that the goal is not 'sweet!' or 'hot!' but 「美味かった。また来るよ！」. It is equally blunt about buying: meat from western Japan, branded eggs, vegetables chosen nationally by season, and a spice blend so complicated that 「作っている本人が間違えてしまうくらいの種類の調合」; wholesalers, it says, complain about how hard the company is on sourcing and on price. The chain went from this room to 97 shops by January 2023 and has since added dozens more, including San Francisco, San Jose and Berkeley in California, Qingdao, and Kaohsiung. Its retort-pouch curry range won a Gold Award at OMOTENASHI Selection 2025. The honten is 19 seats — 11 at the counter, 8 at tables — cash only, all non-smoking, no reservations, with takeaway; it is the branch that still serves chūka-soba and tsukemen alongside the curry, which the company site treats as part of the same craft: 「中華そばのスープ。カレーのルウも日乃屋ならではの手法が用いられております」.
chef_bio.philosophy: 始まり甘く、後より辛い、余韻残りしカレールウ — and beyond the taste, getting the customer to 「美味かった。また来るよ！」 rather than merely to a reaction.
chef_bio.specialty: 名物カツカレー — the katsu curry the chain is known for, now also in a 三元豚・プレミアムカツカレー version; the newer 印度式カレー roux at selected branches; and, at the honten specifically, 中華そば and つけ麺.

anecdotes.text: The head office of a hundred-shop chain is still the counter it started at: the company's 会社概要 gives its 所在地 as 〒113-0034 東京都文京区湯島2-2-1 東邦深澤ビル1階 — the honten's address.
On sourcing, the company quotes its own suppliers against itself: 「日乃屋さんは仕入れうるさいからね（値段交渉も）…」と問屋さんから泣かれることもあります.
The chain's retort-pouch curry took a Gold Award at OMOTENASHI Selection 2025, and the pouches are sold over the counter as souvenirs at a growing number of branches.

cultural_comfort.level: Very easy — but cash, and a walk
cultural_comfort.note: Six minutes north of JR Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit, past Yushima Seidō — a pleasant walk but further than the 御茶ノ水駅周辺 label suggests, and in Bunkyō-ku rather than Chiyoda. Nineteen seats, no reservations, takeaway available, and cash only: no cards, no electronic money, no QR payment. Closed Sundays and public holidays, with occasional unscheduled closures (不定休有), a 15:00 finish on Saturdays and a 15:00–17:00 break on Mondays; last orders are half an hour before closing. There is an English section on the brand site (HINOYA CURRY (ENGLISH)) even though the honten itself does not advertise an English menu, and curry ordering is simple enough that language is rarely the obstacle. If you want the chain's newer 印度式カレー roux, ring first — the company says availability varies by branch. Retort-pouch curry is sold over the counter and makes a genuinely good souvenir.

name: 神保町 黒須

cuisine: For six and a half years the most decorated shōyu-ramen counter in Jimbōchō — seven seats down an alley between the Jōnan Shinkin bank and the Shūeisha building, a Michelin Bib Gourmand three years running and a Tabelog Ramen Hyakumeiten pick four years running, with the 味玉塩蕎麦 at ¥1,300 the bowl reviewers named. It closed on 30 April 2023.

It sat at the end of a narrow alley in the gap between the Jōnan Shinkin Bank and the Shūeisha building.

chef_bio.chef_name: 黒須 (Kurosu) — the Instagram account for the shop, @jinbouchou_kurosu, carries the display name 黒須太一, so the given name is probably Taichi; no source found states it in running text, so treat the surname as certain and the given name as probable
chef_bio.background: 神保町 黒須 opened on 1 November 2016 in a seven-seat, counter-only room reached down a narrow alley between the Jōnan Shinkin Bank and the Shūeisha building — Tabelog files it under 隠れ家レストラン and 一軒家レストラン, which for once is literal. Its owner had come to public notice as one of the last two contestants in the ramen edition of 有吉ジャポン's 成り上がりジャポン before opening here. What followed was one of the fastest reputations in Tokyo ramen: Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and selection as a Tabelog Ramen TOKYO Hyakumeiten in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 — four consecutive years — finishing at 3.90 over 1,918 reviews with 58,000 saves. The bowls reviewers wrote about were the 醤油蕎麦 and the 塩蕎麦, the latter with an ajitama at ¥1,300. It served mornings only, 10:30 to 15:00, six days a week, cash only, all non-smoking, seven seats, no cards of any kind. It shut on 30 April 2023. Reviewers who went on the last day recorded it as a relocation rather than an ending — 「移転の…」 — and one who returned on 1 May found the shop stripped with no notice on the door and the fittings passed to a restaurant-transfer company. Three years on, no shop under this name or this owner appears anywhere on Tabelog, the old domain jinbochoukurosu.net answers with an empty body, and the closure has to be treated as permanent.
chef_bio.specialty: 醤油蕎麦 and 味玉塩蕎麦 (¥1,300) — clear, precise shōyu and shio bowls, the ones every Hyakumeiten citation named.

anecdotes.text: A regular reviewer summed the record up on the final day: 「2016年11月創業後、ミシュラン東京に３年連続選出！食べログのラーメン百名店に４年連続選出の行列店『神保町 黒須』が 2023年4月30日をもって閉店します！」
Another went back the morning after: 「5月1日午前中に店舗跡に足を運ぶ。閉店告知はないが全てが終わった後との雰囲気が漂い、もの寂しい気持ちとなる。」 There was no closing notice on the door at all.
Finding it was part of the experience — Tabelog's own directions read 「城南信用金庫と集英社のビルの隙間にある狭い路地の奥にある」.

chef_bio.origin: Born in Tokyo in 1975; spent ages six to ten in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on his parents' posting
chef_bio.background: 可以 is the second shop of 渡なべ, the Takadanobaba ramen-ya that made 渡辺樹庵's name, and it opened on 2 March 2010 in the premises vacated by めん鳥. Watanabe is an unusual figure in Tokyo ramen: not a chef who came up through a kitchen, but a self-taught obsessive turned consultant. Born in Tokyo in 1975 and a graduate of Meiji Gakuin's economics faculty, he was hit at sixteen by a bowl at Shibuya's げんこつ屋 found through a Tokyo Walker feature — 「こんなに美味しいラーメンがあるのか！」 — started eating his way around the city, and by seventeen was making ramen at home, taking his cues from 永福町大勝軒. By his early twenties he had eaten at more than 2,000 shops nationwide (he now puts the running total past 10,000 bowls). While still a student he fell in with 松田澄夫 of 旭川ラーメン 松楽 and was asked to produce the shop; he renovated it as 麺や 楽 in Isehara in July 2001, produced ラーメン 横綱 in Koshigaya in April 2002, and opened his own 渡なべ in Takadanobaba the same month. The group now runs 渡なべ, 神保町 可以, 六坊担担面 in Ikebukuro and 札幌 六坊, opened in Takadanobaba in April 2025, alongside a long list of produced shops and a 独立開業 programme with named alumni. 可以 originally led on a 2色つけめん; it has since rebuilt itself around 新潟燕三条系背脂煮干し, with the two-colour tsukemen kept on in parallel — a reviewer's judgement on the switch is that 「渡辺樹庵氏プロデュースのご当地ラーメンは、かなり現地っぽさを上手く引き出してイイ感じの着地点に纏めてくる」, that his regional bowls get genuinely close to the originals. The room is a twelve-seat L-shaped counter, dark and calm in the group's house style, behind a glass front at the back of a small setback; ordering is by ticket machine to the right of the door and it is cash only. Tabelog rates it 3.71.
chef_bio.specialty: 背脂煮干しラーメン in the 燕三条 style — reviewers order it 味玉 (a marinated egg version was ¥850 at the time of the review cited, against a sub-¥1,000 band on Tabelog today). The older 2色つけめん is still available, and Niigata regional bowls such as 長岡生姜醤油ラーメン run as limiteds.

anecdotes.text: A reviewer's description of the bowl is the clearest published account of what the shop is now doing: a very hot broth under back fat and lard, with the sardine arriving late — 「煮干しの香りが後発的にジワジワ押し寄せて来る感じで、煮干感は結構強めでビター感を伴うちょっとワイルドな味わい」 — over 緩く縮れた平打ち極太麺, with two slices of 肩ロース chāshū, crunchy menma and coarsely chopped raw onion.
The same reviewer went specifically because the group keeps trading over New Year — 「『渡なべ』系列は正月でも結構営業してたよな！」 — which is how a lot of Tokyo ramen fans first find 可以.

Watanabe's own timeline dates his conversion precisely: aged sixteen, in his first year of high school, he read a Tokyo Walker ramen feature, went to げんこつ屋 in Shibuya, and started eating his way round the country.

Buy a ticket from the machine on the right as you enter. Cash only, no reservations, twelve counter seats — but this is a calm, dark, well-kept room rather than a queue-and-shout ramen bar, and it is comfortable to sit alone in. Hours are a straightforward 11:00–20:00 with no fixed closing day, which is unusually convenient, but unscheduled closures are announced only on X (@jimbocho_kai), so check that before a special trip. name: ラドリオ
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-3
cuisine: The 1949 half-timbered kissaten down an alley off Jimbōchō's book street, dark brown and lit low, chanson on the speakers and paintings that regulars left instead of paying for their coffee. It is where Japan's ウィンナーコーヒー was invented — hot coffee capped with a lid of cold whipped cream — and the food is two dishes: a hard-fried, Tabasco-and-black-pepper Napolitan and a tomato-and-demi-glace chicken curry. About ¥1,000–¥1,999; alcohol all day, with a ¥200 cover if you drink.
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme — 156 m and 2 minutes from Jimbōchō station exit A7 (Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon, Toei Shinjuku and Toei Mita lines), in the alley near Sanseidō's main store.
gf_detail: For food, no — both dishes are out. The Napolitan is wheat pasta, fried hard in a tomato sauce cut with Tabasco and black pepper. The chicken curry, on the recipe left by the manager who created it in 2004, is built on tomato and demi-glace sauce — a demi-glace is a wheat-flour roux by construction — and Japanese curry roux is flour-thickened anyway. There is no allergen information, no gluten-free item and no substitution. What is fine is the drinking: the coffee, including the wienna coffee, and the whisky and cocktails carry no gluten risk beyond the obvious (skip anything beer- or barley-based). Treat it as a place to have a coffee, not a meal, if you cannot have wheat.
vegan_detail: No. The house drink is defined by dairy — the whole point of the wienna coffee is a lid of cold whipped cream — and both food dishes are animal: a chicken curry, and a Napolitan, which in this idiom carries ham or sausage. Nothing plant-based is listed. Black coffee and the spirits are incidentally vegan, but there is no vegan meal here and no plant milk is advertised.

chef_bio.chef_name: 島崎八郎 (Hachirō Shimazaki) — founder; 臼井愛子 (Aiko Usui) — first mama and inventor of the house wienna coffee
roles: 初代ママ (first mama, 臼井愛子, who also served as vice-chair of the bartenders' association)
店長 (a succession of managers since, changing every few years)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Jimbōchō, Chiyoda-ku — the founder's antiquarian bookshop stood nearby from 1939, and he bought the building the café occupies, living on the first floor above it
chef_bio.background: ラドリオ was opened in October 1949 by 島崎八郎, a Tokyo University economics graduate who became a banker, found the salary insufficient, and opened the second-hand bookshop 島崎書店 in front of the Akamon gate at Hongō — selling social science and foreign-language books, and the work of his younger brother, the novelist 島木健作. He opened a Jimbōchō branch in 1939 opposite the Kanda Nikkatsu cinema; the Hongō shop burned in the Tokyo air raids and Jimbōchō became the whole business. Wanting 「本を読みながらコーヒーや酒が飲める場所」 — somewhere you could read with a coffee or a drink — he bought a building near the shop, put a café on the ground floor and his home above it. The name is Spanish for brick, ladrillo; the half-timbering was the fashion of the year it opened, and the bricks are said to be the same as those of Tokyo Station's Marunouchi building and the Ōji mint. Inside is dark brown and low-lit, with a brick counter, wooden chairs of deliberately uneven height, a red sofa and a stove in use since opening. The chanson on the speakers is the taste of the first mama, 臼井愛子, the founder's niece, who also invented the shop's wienna coffee — cold whipped cream floated as a lid over hot coffee, from a regular Tokyo University professor's description of a coffee he had drunk in Vienna, combined with a cream-topped cake she saw while walking in Kanda-Ogawamachi, and the practical need to stop the coffee going cold during long arguments. Usui was vice-chair of the bartenders' association and the cocktails she made are still served; she left in 1996. Artists paid in pictures, which is why the walls carry the work they left, and the cow that appears on the shop's cups, matches and ashtrays was drawn by the sculptor 本郷新. The list of people who used it as an office is a literary map of postwar Tokyo: 伊達得夫 ran the magazine ユリイカ from across the alley and used ラドリオ as his reception room 「毎日三時間くらいは腰をおろしている」; 片岡義男 wrote at the window two-seater every day; 逢坂剛 took the phone call telling him he had won the 1986 Naoki Prize for 『カディスの赤い星』 standing in the shop; 川端康成, 三島由紀夫, 田村隆一, 草野心平, 埴谷雄高 and others passed through. The founder also ran the neighbouring ミロンガ (now ミロンガ・ヌオーバ), and the owner of さぼうる, 鈴木文雄, has said that ラドリオ was his model — 「『ラドリオ』が目標だったから何度も通って勉強した」 — and copied its half-timbering. In 2000 the leaning building was jacked up, its columns replaced and the brick floor raised about ten centimetres. Managers have rotated every few years since; one of them started the monthly ラドリオかわら版, a staff-made newsletter of Jimbōchō trivia still handed out. The room seats 49 (7 at the counter, 42 at tables) and Tabelog rates it 3.71.
chef_bio.philosophy: The founder's original brief, unchanged since 1949: 「本を読みながらコーヒーや酒が飲める場所」 — a place to drink coffee or alcohol while you read.
chef_bio.specialty: ウィンナーコーヒー — the house invention, hot coffee under a lid of cold whipped cream; ナポリタン, noodles cooked firm and fried until the water is driven out, sauced with tomato, Tabasco and black pepper; チキンカレー on the 2004 recipe, mild, tomato and demi-glace based.

anecdotes.text: The wienna coffee was reverse-engineered from hearsay. A regular who was a Tokyo University professor described a coffee with something white on it that he had drunk in Vienna; the mama imagined her way toward it and got the answer from a cream-topped cake she spotted while walking through Kanda-Ogawamachi.
It was also a practical fix — the shop was much bigger in 1949, coffee took a long time to reach the table, and debates ran hot; a cap of whipped cream kept the cup from going cold.
The pictures on the walls are unpaid bills. Artists brought in work and sometimes left it in place of the price of a coffee.
逢坂剛 had been coming since he was a student at Chūō University; in 1986 he was standing in the shop when the call came that 『カディスの赤い星』 had won the Naoki Prize.
伊達得夫 edited ユリイカ from a room so cramped that he used the café as his meeting room: 「ラドリオの椅子に毎日三時間くらいは腰をおろしている。ぼくに向い合っている人は、毎日違うのだ。」

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13006555 lists ラドリオ（LADRIO）under 神保町/喫茶店・バー・カフェ at 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-3, tel 03-3295-4788, coordinates 35.69565/139.75981, 2 minutes and 156 m from Jimbōchō station, 49 seats (7 counter, 42 table), 予約不可, cash only with no cards, electronic money or QR payment, all non-smoking, no service charge but a ¥200 otōshi when alcohol is ordered, hours 11:30–22:30 (L.O. 22:00) Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri and 12:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:30) weekends and holidays, closed Tuesdays, an opening year of 1949, a ¥1,000–¥1,999 band, a 3.71 rating, official accounts on Facebook and instagram.com/ladrio1949, and a note that the seventh manager retired in April 2023. Its PR line reads 「『神保町』三省堂本店近くの路地にある歴史のあるお店。シャンソンが流れるクラシックな装いのカフェバー。」 The Japanese Wikipedia article on ラドリオ, which is heavily footnoted to books and newspaper coverage (川口 2015, 塩沢 2009, 佐藤 2015, 下里 2005/2018, 読売新聞社 2018 and others), supplies the founding history, the Spanish etymology, the half-timbering and brick provenance, the interior description, the invention and purpose of the wienna coffee, the chanson and cocktail inheritance from 臼井愛子, the 本郷新 cow logo, the roll-call of writer regulars, the relationship to ミロンガ・ヌオーバ and さぼうる, the 2000 jacking-up of the building, the ラドリオかわら版 newsletter, the Napolitan and chicken-curry specifications, and the A7-exit access.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Both food items are wheat — a fried Napolitan and a demi-glace-based curry — cooked in one small kitchen. No allergen information is published and no gluten-free option exists.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house drink is defined by whipped cream, and the two dishes are a chicken curry and a Napolitan. No plant milk or plant-based dish is advertised.

positives.text: Coffee, whisky and the house cocktails are all served all day, so a wheat-avoiding visitor can sit here for hours without going near the kitchen — which, for a shop whose whole point is sitting and reading, is most of the experience.

cultural_comfort.level: Very easy, and worth going even if you only drink coffee
cultural_comfort.note: Two minutes from Jimbōchō exit A7, in an alley near Sanseidō's main store — look for the half-timbered front, since the door is easy to walk past. Forty-nine seats, no reservations, all non-smoking, children welcome. Cash only: no cards, no IC, no QR. There is no service charge, but ordering alcohol brings a ¥200 otōshi. Closed Tuesdays; note the split schedule — Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri run 11:30 to 22:30, but weekends and public holidays close at 19:00. Nobody will hurry you: this has been a place to sit and read since 1949 and people still do. Order the ウィンナーコーヒー at least once — it was invented in this room, and the cold cream lid over hot coffee is the point rather than a garnish. Pick up the ラドリオかわら版, the staff-made monthly sheet of Jimbōchō trivia, on the way out. No English menu, but the drink names are largely katakana and the two food dishes are Napolitan and chicken curry.
